signals.title: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger Begin Formal Withdrawal From ICC
signals.summary: [Shabelle] Ouagadougou -- Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger have formally launched the process of withdrawing from the International Criminal Court (ICC) after submitting official notifications to leave the Rome Statute, according to a statement from the Assembly of States Parties to the court.

signals.title: World Bank Group Appoints Nicola Pontara As Division Director for Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali and Niger
signals.summary: [World Bank] Bamako -- The World Bank Group has announced the appointment of Nicola Pontara as Division Director for the Sahel countries - Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, and Chad.

signals.title: Senegal MPs Pass Reform Limiting Presidential Powers
signals.summary: [allAfrica] The parliament has approved controversial constitutional reforms that expand lawmakers' powers while limiting those of the president, deepening a growing rift between President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and parliamentary Speaker Ousmane Sonko.

signals.title: France – Burkina Faso : Jean-Noël Barrot et Karamoko Jean-Marie Traoré, ministres au cœur de la rupture
signals.summary: La rupture entre Paris et Ouagadougou est désormais consommée. Aboutissement logique d’une crise diplomatique qui ne cessait de s’accentuer, elle a été prononcée, de part et d’autre, par deux ministres qui ne s’apprécient guère.

signals.title: President Tinubu Congratulates Kabir Shagaya At 40
signals.summary: [State Department] President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, has congratulated Mr Kabir Shagaya, Director of Strategy at Cavista Holdings, on his 40th birthday, commending his contributions to enterprise development, strategic investment, innovation, and national development.

signals.title: UK Backs Kenya As Regional Security Anchor, Eyes New Frontiers in Cyber and Ai
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The United Kingdom is deepening its security partnership with Kenya beyond traditional counterterrorism operations to tackle emerging threats including cybercrime, artificial intelligence (AI) risks and organised immigration crime, British High Commissioner to Kenya Matt Baugh has said.

signals.title: UK, Kenya Begin Talks On Landmark Digital Trade Deal to Boost E-Commerce, Tech Investment
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The United Kingdom and Kenya have begun negotiations on a landmark Digital Trade Agreement aimed at expanding cross-border digital commerce, reducing barriers for businesses and cementing Kenya's position as Africa's "Silicon Savannah," British High Commissioner to Kenya Matt Baugh has revealed.

signals.title: NPS Warns Political Actors Against Violence, Says No One Is Above the Law
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The National Police Service (NPS) has warned political actors and their supporters against engaging in violence and disrupting lawful gatherings, insisting that no individual or political affiliation is above the law.

signals.title: 19-Year-Old Woman Dies After Falling From Fifth Floor Building in Kayole
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Police in Kayole are investigating the death of a 19-year-old woman who fell from the fifth floor of a residential building in Nairobi's Kayole area.

signals.title: Fresh Fears in Oyo As Gunmen Kidnap School Headmaster
signals.summary: [Premium Times] Mr Owoade, who is also a member of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), was abducted around 6:00 p.m. on Saturday while returning home from his farm in Budo Aare, Itesiwaju Local Government Area of the state.

signals.title: Court Rules No Automatic Renewal for State CEOs
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Court of Appeal has dismissed an appeal by former Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Managing Director Jadiah Mwarania, ruling that he had no automatic right or legitimate expectation to a third five-year term after the expiry of his contract.

signals.title: Gunmen Kidnap Oyo School Headmaster, Demand N30m Ransom
signals.summary: [Vanguard] A 60-year-old headmaster of Nomadic Basic School, Igbojaye, in Itesiwaju Local Government Area of Oyo State, Mr Matthew Kolawale Owoade, popularly known as "Onaiye", has allegedly been abducted by unidentified gunmen.

signals.title: Court Reserves Judgment in Suit Challenging Pantami As Gombe PDP Governorship Candidate
signals.summary: [Premium Times] Mr Pantami defected from the APC after losing out in that party's governorship primary, citing irregularities and injustice.

signals.title: High Court Summons Lenku in Amboseli Park Contempt Case
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Kajiado Governor Joseph Ole Lenku faces a possible six-month jail term after the High Court summoned him to appear on July 24 to answer contempt proceedings over allegations that he defied conservatory orders suspending the transfer of Amboseli National Park to the Kajiado County Government.

signals.title: Uganda: Court clears way for Besigye treason trial
signals.summary: The High Court has dismissed an application by Dr. Kizza Besigye and Hajji Obeid Lutale seeking to terminate treason proceedings, clearing the way for their trial to begin on July 13, 2026. The court ruled the application lacked merit and was intended to delay the criminal case.

signals.title: US-Africa Week Ahead: Trump’s Africa envoy heads to West Africa as Washington courts Sahel juntas
signals.summary: Assistant Secretary of State Frank Garcia is travelling to Nigeria, Mali and Côte d’Ivoire for his inaugural trip to the continent, as the United States seeks to rebuild ties with the Alliance of Sahelian States.

signals.title: Premiers ministrables marocains : ceux que l’opinion plébiscite
signals.summary: Aucun d’entre eux ne dirige un grand parti, et certains n’ont même jamais exprimé leur désir d’occuper le poste de chef du gouvernement. Pourtant, leur nom revient avec insistance dès qu’il est question du Maroc de l’après 2026.

signals.title: Ruto Tops New Presidential Poll At 32% As Kalonzo Comes Second At 13% - Infotrak
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- President William Ruto would retain the presidency if elections were held today, according to a new Infotrak Research and Consulting survey that places him ahead of his closest rivals in the race to State House.

signals.title: 14 Charged Over Kisumu, Nyahururu Violence As Police Vow Tough Crackdown
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Fourteen suspects have been arraigned over weekend violence in Kisumu and Nyahururu as the government faces growing pressure to demonstrate that its repeated pledges to end political goonism will be backed by consistent prosecutions rather than rhetoric.

signals.title: Plateau, Benue Killings - Nigeria Cannot Prosper While Innocent Blood Flows - Obi
signals.summary: [Vanguard] Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 election, has condemned the latest killings in Benue and Plateau states, saying Nigeria cannot achieve meaningful development while innocent citizens continue to lose their lives to violence.

signals.title: ICPC Arraigns Ex-Minister Uche Nnaji for Certificate Forgery, Misappropriation of Funds
signals.summary: [Premium Times] ICPC arraigned the 63-year-old Nnaji on six charges before Judge Joyce Abdulmalik of the Federal High Court in Abuja.

signals.title: Nigeria Meets 104% of OPEC Quota As Production Soars
signals.summary: [Premium Times] According to the crude statistics, released by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) on Sunday, in the month under review, crude oil production hit 1. 56 million barrels per day (mbpd)

signals.title: Ex-Minister Uche Nnaji Arrives Court to Face Arraignment for Certificate Forgery
signals.summary: [Premium Times] The ICPC is expected to arraign the former minister on charges of forgery and making false statements in documents submitted to public authorities.

signals.title: Ramaphosa honors South Africa's WWI fallen in France
signals.summary: Ramaphosa also called for greater recognition of Black South Africans whose contributions to the war were ignored for decades, saying the country's history should reflect the sacrifice of all who served.

signals.title: Senegal coach Pape Thiaw sacked after World Cup exit
signals.summary: Senegal's national footbal coach Pape Thiaw's functions were revoked in the night from Sunday to Monday. The decision is "in the best interests of Senegalese football", according to the Senegalese Football Federation.

signals.title: Nigeria : le soulagement des parents après la libération d'élèves enlevés
signals.summary: Au Nigeria, les enlèvements dans les écoles sont fréquents. Des groupes armés les prennent pour cible afin de faire pression sur le gouvernement et d’obtenir des rançons.

signals.title: Oyo Abduction - the Rescue Was Successful, but Where Was the Noise?
signals.summary: [Vanguard] When the news first broke that students and teachers had been abducted, the nation reacted as expected. Social media erupted with outrage. Television stations ran breaking news coverage. Newspapers led with banner headlines. Political commentators dissected the incident, while citizens demanded answers from the government and security agencies.

signals.title: Detained Oriire Terrorists' Wives May Face Trial, Calls Mount for Borno Pupils' Rescue
signals.summary: [Leadership] Some wives of suspected terrorists behind the abduction of schoolchildren and teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State may face prosecution if ongoing investigations establish that they played active roles in the kidnapping operation, security sources have disclosed.

signals.title: Paul Biya et le Cameroun : d’un 13 juillet à l’autre, chronique d’une année folle
signals.summary: Le 13 juillet 2025, Paul Biya mettait fin à un faux suspense, déclarant sa candidature à la présidentielle, 43 ans après son arrivée au pouvoir. Le début d’une surprenante campagne électorale et d’une étrange année politique, à l’issue de laquelle la nouvelle ère attendue n’est toujours pas advenue.

signals.title: Govt Arrests Two Suspected Illegal Miners, Shuts Osun Mining Site
signals.summary: [Premium Times] According to the federal government, the suspects are assisting investigators to identify the sponsors of the illegal mining operation as authorities intensify efforts to curb unlawful mineral exploitation.

signals.title: Enhancing the Integrity of the 2026 Electoral Act
signals.summary: [Premium Times] Our federal lawmakers deserve a strong rebuke for these bizarre contrivances to the legislation taking us into the next general elections.

signals.title: CJ Koome Establishes High Court Division to Handle Tribunal Appeals
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Chief Justice Martha Koome has established a new Tribunals Appeals Division of the High Court at the Milimani Law Courts in Nairobi in a move aimed at improving access to justice and expediting the resolution of disputes arising from specialised tribunals.

signals.title: LSK Condemns Violence Ahead of Ol Kalou By-Election, Deploys Election Observers
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) has condemned all forms of violence, intimidation, incitement and lawlessness ahead of the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, warning that such actions threaten constitutional rights and democratic participation.

signals.title: Govt Moves to Suspend Sh6.9tn Public Debt Case
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Attorney General has asked the High Court to suspend proceedings in a petition challenging the government's management of more than Sh6.9 trillion in public debt, arguing that the issues raised are already the subject of an ongoing forensic audit.

signals.title: Police Seize 3,860 Litres of Illicit Brew, Arrest Four in Kahawa West Crackdown
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Police have seized 3,860 litres of illicit alcohol and arrested four suspects following a raid on an illegal brewing den in the Soweto area of Kahawa West, as authorities intensify efforts to dismantle illicit alcohol production networks.

signals.title: No Region Will Be Marginalised, President Ruto Assures Kenyans
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Kitui -- President William Ruto has assured Kenyans that every part of the country will receive its fair share of development regardless of political affiliation or voting patterns.

signals.title: Wetang'ula Urges Bungoma Residents to Back Ruto's 2027 Re-Election Bid
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula has urged residents of Bungoma County to support President William Ruto's re-election in 2027, saying the Kenya Kwanza administration has fulfilled key development pledges that are transforming lives across the region.

signals.title: Police Deny Claims Kang'ata Driver Was Shot During Nyahururu Violence
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The National Police Service has dismissed claims that the driver of Murang'a Governor Irungu Kang'ata was shot during political violence that erupted in Nyahururu.

signals.title: IEBC Summons Gikaria Over Alleged Voter Bribery in Ol Kalou By-Election Campaign
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Nakuru Town East Member of Parliament David Gikaria is set to appear before the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee over allegations of voter bribery during campaigns for the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election.

signals.title: Procès de Kizza Besigye: «Il existe une instrumentalisation du système judiciaire en Ouganda»
signals.summary: C'est ce lundi 13 juillet que doit s'ouvrir en Ouganda le procès du docteur Kizza Besigye, 70 ans, qui est l'opposant historique au président Museveni. Pour sa défense, ses avocats ne vont pas manquer de rappeler qu’en novembre 2024, Kizza Besigye a été kidnappé au Kenya puis livré à l'Ouganda. Peut-on parler, comme notre invitée de ce matin, d'une « est-africanisation » de la répression ? Florence Brisset-Foucault est maîtresse de conférence en sciences politiques à…

signals.title: Parents in southwestern Nigeria relieved after kidnapped children return
signals.summary: Parents of students abducted from a school in Nigeria's southwestern Oyo State expressed relief and gratitude after their children were rescued following nearly two months in captivity.

signals.title: Shettima's Retention Signals APC's Strength in North, Youth Parliament Declares
signals.summary: [Leadership] The APC Youth Parliament has expressed confidence that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's decision to retain vice president Kashim Shettima as his running mate for the 2027 general elections will strengthen the ruling party's chances of victory, particularly in the North-East and the Northern region.

signals.title: Court Restricts Lawyers in Police Force but Not Appointed As Legal Officers to Only Prosecution
signals.summary: [Premium Times] The judge also ordered the police force, Police Service Commission (PSC) and the Inspector-General of the Federation to deploy "police officers who are legal practitioners to every Police Division in Nigeria to assist with the enforcement of human rights in policing at the Divisions."

signals.title: Dangote Cracks Down On Illegal Haulage, Offers N500,000 Reward for Whistleblowers
signals.summary: [Vanguard] Dangote Industries Limited has intensified efforts to combat illegal haulage activities involving its trucks by unveiling a public whistleblowing initiative that offers a cash reward to individuals who provide credible information leading to the arrest of offenders or the interception of unauthorized goods and transportation of persons.

signals.title: Alledged Wrong Parking - Why Peter Obi May Not Apologise, Pay N25,000 Airport Fine - Udim
signals.summary: [Vanguard] Senior Partner at Justice Chambers, Ekemini Udim, has identified reasons why the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, may not apologise to airport officials and pay a N25,000 fine over an alleged parking violation at the Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport, Abuja.

signals.title: State Police, President Tinubu's Masterstroke Against Insecurity, Says Dep. Senate President Barau
signals.summary: [This Day] The Deputy President of the Senate and Chairman of the Senate Committee on Constitution Review, Senator Barau I. Jibrin, has described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's quest to establish State Police as a "masterstroke" aimed at decisively addressing insecurity in the country.

signals.title: No Info About Our 78 Children Kidnapped By Boko Haram Weeks Ago, Parents Lament
signals.summary: [Leadership] Parents of the 42 Mussa Primary and Junior Secondary School pupils and students, as well as the 36 Lassa Government Day Secondary School Students,in Askira-Uba local government area of Borno State, still in the hands of the Boko Haram terrorists weeks after their abduction, have gone spiritual seeking God's intervention over the safe return of their children.

signals.title: Omollo - Churches Must Unite Kenyans, Not Promote Politics of Division
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Homa Bay -- Principal Secretary for Internal Security and National Administration Raymond Omollo has urged churches to remain places of worship and unity rather than platforms for political leaders to spread hatred, tribalism and division.

signals.title: IEBC Intensifies Preparations Ahead of Thursday's Ol Kalou Parliamentary By-Election
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) says preparations for Thursday's Ol Kalou Parliamentary by-election are in the final stages, with the training of key election officials already completed.

signals.title: Seven Held After Thika Raid Uncovers Illicit Ethanol, Fake Cigarettes
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Police have arrested seven people after a multi-agency operation in Thika West Sub-County uncovered 13,200 litres of ethanol and thousands of packets of suspected counterfeit cigarettes.

signals.title: CS Mutua Hails Ruto As 'Kenya's Messi and Mbappé' During Kitui Tour
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Kitui -- Cabinet Secretary Alfred Mutua has likened President William Ruto to football superstars Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappé, praising the Head of State's leadership and development agenda during his tour of Kitui County.

signals.title: Sh350bn National Infrastructure Fund Will Drive Kenya's Transformation - Ruto
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Kitui -- President William Ruto has said the Sh350 billion mobilised through the newly established National Infrastructure Fund (NIF) will play a critical role in financing major development projects and accelerating Kenya's transition into a first-world economy.

signals.title: Ruto Urges Kenyans to Reject Divisive Politics As Government Accelerates Development Projects in Kitui
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- President William Ruto has urged Kenyans to reject leaders promoting divisive politics, saying national unity is essential for the country to achieve its development goals.

signals.title: Centrafrique: le climat d'insécurité préoccupe les habitants de certains quartiers de Bangui
signals.summary: Les cas de braquage se multiplient ces dernières semaines dans plusieurs quartiers de Bangui. Malgré le renforcement des patrouilles des forces de sécurité intérieure et l’interpellation d’une dizaine de présumés braqueurs, les habitants estiment que la menace reste bien présente.

signals.title: Maroc: le système de santé face au défi des vagues de chaleur récurrentes
signals.summary: Le Maroc vient de vivre une nouvelle vague de chaleur intense sur pratiquement l’ensemble de son territoire, avec des températures frôlant les 50 degrés à certains endroits. Pourtant, le royaume n’est toujours pas davantage préparé.

signals.title: Nigeria Designed the Cure for Its Electricity Crisis. It Stopped Administering It Halfway.
signals.summary: [African Arguments] Ask anyone who has lived in Nigeria what NEPA stands for, and they will tell you it stands for Never Expect Power Always. The National Electric Power Authority (NEPA) was the state monopoly that, for decades, generated the country's electricity, carried it across the country, and sold it to Nigerians, badly. The joke outlived the institution, but the problem it named did not. The generators still hum outside shops and homes, and the grid still delivers…

signals.title: Madagascar: forte inquiétude à Antananarivo après une vague de disparitions
signals.summary: À Madagascar, la vague de disparitions en cours depuis fin juin plonge Antananarivo dans un état de psychose. Le dernier bilan communiqué par la police nationale la semaine passée fait état de 91 enfants toujours recherchés à travers le pays. La plupart des signalements concernent la capitale où les habitants, angoissés, changent leurs habitudes en évitant par exemple de sortir seuls dehors.

signals.title: Mozambique: rapport d'Acled sur les «nouvelles stratégies» de l'EI dans le Cabo Delgado
signals.summary: « Comment l'État islamique construit son bastion au Mozambique ? » C'est l'objet du rapport de l'organisation ACLED sur les « nouvelles stratégies » du groupe terroriste dans la province du Cabo Delgado. Implantés sur une zone qui s'étend sur plus de 100 km le long de la côte et 50 km vers les terres, les insurgés cherchent à conquérir une « légitimité sociale » auprès des habitants. Acled pointe une approche moins violente de la part du groupe terroriste, afin de gagner…

signals.title: Or: la redistribution des investissements rebat les cartes en Afrique de l'Ouest
signals.summary: Alors que le Mali, le Burkina Faso et le Ghana renforcent leur contrôle sur leur secteur aurifère, les compagnies minières internationales réorientent leurs investissements vers des pays jugés plus prévisibles. La Côte d'Ivoire, la Guinée, mais aussi la Mauritanie et le Sénégal espèrent profiter de cette redistribution.

signals.title: Créer en langues africaines: Nigeria, littérature en yoruba et roman fondateur de D.O. Fagunwa [1/5]
signals.summary: 50 millions de personnes parlent yoruba à travers les pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest et leurs diasporas. C’est une langue essentiellement orale mais qui possède tout de même des œuvres littéraires. Daniel Olorunfemi Fagunwa publie le premier roman en langue autochtone en 1938, à une époque où seule la Bible était disponible en langue locale. Aujourd’hui, des acteurs de la culture œuvrent pour entretenir et encourager une production littéraire.

signals.title: Sommet sur les minerais critiques à Abidjan : l'Afrique veut transformer davantage
signals.summary: Longtemps cantonnée au rôle de fournisseur de matières premières, l’Afrique veut désormais transformer davantage de ses minerais sur son propre sol. Cobalt, lithium, graphite ou encore cuivre sont au cœur de la transition énergétique mondiale. À Abidjan, responsables politiques, industriels et investisseurs réfléchissent aux moyens de développer des chaînes de valeur locales et de capter une plus grande part des richesses générées par ces ressources.

signals.title: Afrique du Sud : pourquoi les violences contre les migrants africains se multiplient-elles ?
signals.summary: Pourquoi les violences contre les migrants africains connaissent-elles un regain en Afrique du Sud ? Depuis plusieurs mois, commerces pillés, familles déplacées et manifestations anti-immigration se multiplient. Dans cet entretien, le géographe Philippe Gervais-Lambony, spécialiste de l'Afrique du Sud depuis plus de trente ans, analyse les racines de cette crise : héritage de l'apartheid, inégalités, chômage, discours politiques et montée des mouvements xénophobes.

signals.title: South Africa says more than 53,000 foreigners deported in migration campaign
signals.summary: South Africa is cracking down on undocumented migrants following widespread anti-immigration protests.

signals.title: Gabon: un collectif d’associations dénonce le piratage de groupes WhatsApp
signals.summary: Au Gabon, la suspension des réseaux sociaux, décidée en février dernier, est toujours en vigueur. Cinq mois plus tard, les Gabonais sont obligés d’utiliser les VPN (réseaux privés virtuels) pour se connecter sur Facebook, WhatsApp, YouTube et autres. Malheureusement, un phénomène a surgi : le piratage des comptes Facebook et WhatsApp. Face à la recrudescence de ces actes de piratage, un collectif de cinq ONG et associations a animé, samedi 11 juillet, à Libreville, une…

signals.title: Kenya: MSF trains health workers to be sent to Ebola-hit DR Congo
signals.summary: An Ebola training facility set up by Doctors Without Borders in Kenya is a chance for health workers to prepare for one of the most complex emergencies they are ever likely to face.

signals.title: Qui, aux côtés du colonel Randrianirina, gouverne vraiment Madagascar ?
signals.summary: Autour du colonel-président gravite une garde rapprochée mêlant loyaux camarades de promotion, personnalités recasées et entrepreneurs proches du pouvoir. Ces hommes et femmes de l’ombre dessinent les contours du nouveau régime.

signals.title: Zimbabweans return home from South Africa amid anti-immigrant tensions
signals.summary: Zimbabweans fleeing xenophobic violence and threats in South Africa arrived at a reception centre in the border town of Beitbridge, Zimbabwe

signals.title: Le repreneur de Shell au Nigeria peut-il devenir « le leader africain de l’énergie » ?
signals.summary: Renaissance Africa Energy relance l’exploitation d’un gisement découvert en 1967 mais resté inexploité depuis. Une preuve supplémentaire de la reprise en main locale des ressources du Nigeria.

signals.title: Cobalt, lithium, graphite, cuivre... l’Afrique veut transformer ses minerais sur son propre sol
signals.summary: Longtemps cantonnée au rôle de fournisseur de matières premières, l’Afrique veut désormais transformer davantage de ses minerais sur son propre sol. Cobalt, lithium, graphite ou encore cuivre sont au cœur de la transition énergétique mondiale. À Abidjan, responsables politiques, industriels et investisseurs réfléchissent aux moyens de développer des chaînes de valeur locales et de capter une plus grande part des richesses générées par ces ressources.

signals.title: La Sierra Leone se prépare à accueillir le sommet de la Cédéao, une vitrine diplomatique onéreuse?
signals.summary: En Sierra Leone, les réunions préparatoires du 69e sommet de la Cédéao débutent, ce dimanche 12 juillet, avant la rencontre des chefs d’État prévue dans une semaine le dimanche 19 juillet. C’est la première fois que le pays accueille ce type de sommet régional et les autorités n’ont pas lésiné sur les moyens tels qu’une logistique renforcée, de nouvelles infrastructures et surtout une salle de conférences, construite à Lungi pour l’occasion. Le coût global de l’événement…

signals.title: Senegal sack manager Thiaw in wake of World Cup exit
signals.summary: Senegal sack manager Pape Thiaw in the aftermath of the country's exit at the last-32 stage of the 2026 World Cup.

signals.title: Students abducted in May by Islamic militants in Nigeria recovering, governor says
signals.summary: Students abducted in May by Islamic militants in Nigeria’s southwestern state of Oyo were rescued and receiving medical treatment, confirmed the local government on Friday.

signals.title: Centrafrique: à Am Dafok, de nombreux déplacés et une situation «calme mais imprévisible», selon la Minusca
signals.summary: Dans le nord de la Centrafrique, à la frontière avec le Soudan, une semaine après la reprise par les forces armées centrafricaines de la localité d'Am Dafok le 5 juillet des mains des groupes rebelles, la quasi-totalité de la population de la zone est rassemblée près de la base temporaire de la Minusca. La mission des Nations unies en Centrafrique dit suivre la situation de près.

signals.title: Inside Ruto’s inner circle: Fixers, soldiers and gatekeepers shaping the 2027 race
signals.summary: With just over a year until the next general election, Kenya President William Ruto faces a challenging political landscape as pressure mounts from a unified opposition coalition aiming to unseat him. To secure a second term, Ruto will need maximum support from key allies within the ruling Kenya Kwanza coalition.

signals.title: RDC: un audit signale près de 40% d'agents fictifs ou inactifs dans la police
signals.summary: En République démocratique du Congo, un audit des effectifs de la police nationale met au jour des irrégularités de grande ampleur. Sur 158 000 dossiers examinés, près de 40 % sont jugés suspects. Pour le gouvernement, l'enjeu est aussi financier : ces anomalies pourraient coûter plus de 230 millions de dollars par an.

signals.title: 'Relief' as 44 kidnapped children and teachers freed after Nigerian army operation
signals.summary: "I feel happy and elated… I feel joy," the head of the local teachers' union tells the BBC.

signals.title: Au Nigeria, l’érosion du littoral d’Orimedu menace les villages
signals.summary: Dans cette communauté côtière du golfe de Guinée, la montée du niveau de la mer, le changement climatique et la dégradation des sols accélèrent le recul du rivage. Une exposition itinérante consacrée aux solutions d’adaptation tente de sensibiliser les habitants et les décideurs.

signals.title: Nigeria’s eroding Orimedu coast threatens homes and livelihoods
signals.summary: This coastline along Orimedu in Nigeria is facing land degradation. The people here are seeing the destruction of their homes as well as the loss of livelihoods.

signals.title: SA police arrest UK fugitive sought in alleged killings of his wife and 2 daughters
signals.summary: South African police arrested a man wanted by British authorities on suspicion of killing his wife and two young daughters in England after tracing him to Johannesburg, police said Friday.

signals.title: Comment le Bénin tente de faire face à un afflux inédit de réfugiés sahéliens
signals.summary: Venues du Burkina Faso, du Niger et du Nigeria, des dizaines de milliers de personnes déplacées de force ont rejoint le septentrion béninois. Une crise humanitaire silencieuse qui teste les limites du modèle d’accueil communautaire choisi par Cotonou. Décryptage en infographies.

signals.title: Le Limpopo, miroir de la crise migratoire sud-africaine
signals.summary: Le fleuve Limpopo est devenu le théâtre d’un double mouvement migratoire : des exilés tentent toujours de rejoindre clandestinement l’Afrique du Sud, tandis que des dizaines de milliers d’étrangers repartent après une vague de violences xénophobes.

signals.title: Secrets sécuritaires au Togo, nouvelle offensive jihadiste au Mali, reprise en main des mines au Sénégal… Les 5 infos qu’il ne fallait pas manquer

signals.title: Afrique du Sud : les manifestations anti-migrants font peser un risque sur l'économie

signals.title: Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo’s growing influence in Africa

signals.title: S.Africa minister raises concerns about security at Zimbabwe border
signals.summary: "Something has to be done urgently" about border security at the Limpopo river border with Zimbabwe, says South Africa's minister of Public works and Infrastructure, Dean Macpherson after visiting the area. "It was shocking...there literally is no border in some places," he says.

signals.title: How a fake presidential council ended up with a budget of almost $1m in Nigeria
signals.summary: The government says it was set up with a forged letter of appointment but others say there is more to it.

signals.title: Wanyonyi breaks 1,000m world record on debut in Monaco

signals.title: South African president welcomed by Macron at start of visit to France
signals.summary: Cyril Ramaphosa will also co-chair a UNESCO meeting on education and take part in the 110th anniversary of the Battle of Delville Wood.

signals.title: Rupture Diomaye-Sonko, dette cachée et FMI : le débat « Sans Filtre » sur la situation au Sénégal
signals.summary: Quel rôle la dette cachée a-t-elle joué dans la rupture entre le leader de Pastef, Ousmane Sonko, et son ancien numéro 2 et actuel président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye ? Le tout premier débat « Sans Filtre », nouveau rendez-vous de Jeune Afrique, tente de répondre.

signals.title: Soudan : l'ONU appuie les enquêtes de la CPI sur les crimes de guerre au Darfour
signals.summary: Au Soudan, l’ONU soutient les enquêtes de la CPI sur les crimes de guerre au Darfour. Son envoyé spécial s’est rendu dans des camps de réfugiés à l’est du Tchad. La procureure adjointe de la CPI était aussi sur place.

signals.title: Côte d’Ivoire : entre Abidjan et San Pedro, la SIR a tranché pour sa deuxième raffinerie
signals.summary: Entre la capitale économique et la grande ville du Sud-Ouest, la Société ivoirienne de raffinage a, sauf ultime rebondissement, choisi le territoire qui accueillera sa future installation. Coulisses.

signals.title: Mali : l’Africa Corps et les Fama brisent le siège d’Anéfis
signals.summary: Le verrou d’Anéfis n’a pas cédé. Arrivés en renfort depuis Gao, l’armée malienne et les paramilitaires russes sont parvenus à repousser l’offensive du FLA et du Jnim. Une victoire qui pourrait accélérer la reconquête des bastions rebelles du Nord, dont Kidal et Tessalit.

signals.title: 60 000 migrants ont quitté l'Afrique du Sud depuis début juin
signals.summary: Plus de 38 000 ressortissants malawites ont quitté l’Afrique du Sud en l’espace d’un mois, dans un contexte de tensions croissantes visant les populations étrangères. Les autorités sud-africaines estiment qu’environ 60 000 personnes auraient quitté le pays depuis le début de cette période de crise.

signals.title: En Mauritanie, le paradis menacé de la pêche traditionnelle des Imraguen
signals.summary: C'est un mode de vie multiséculaire qui se transmet de génération en génération. Mais le réchauffement climatique risque d'y mettre fin. On vous propose de passer quelques minutes avec les Imraguen, un peuple de pêcheurs du désert mauritanien, à la jonction entre le Sahara aride et l'océan Atlantique. Récit de Ludovic de Foucaud.

signals.title: Crimes de guerre au Soudan : l'ONU enquête dans les camps de réfugiés du Tchad
signals.summary: La guerre au Soudan impacte directement ses voisins, comme le Tchad, où les Nations Unies ont intensifié le rythme de leurs visites ces derniers mois. L'objectif : trouver une issue à ce conflit. L'envoyé spécial du secrétaire général de l'ONU s'est rendu dans les camps de réfugiés de l'est du pays, tandis que la procureure adjointe de la Cour Pénale Internationale était à N'Djamena. Précisions d’Harold Girard, correspondant de France 24.

signals.title: RD Congo : l'opposition rentre du Burundi après des consultations pour sortir le pay de la crise
signals.summary: Ils sont de retour à Kinshasa après leur visite à Bujumbura dans un contexte de vive tension autour de la révision de la Constitution. Les opposants congolais ont présenté les conclusions des consultations avec le président burundais, Évariste Ndayishimiye, président en exercice de l’Union africaine. À cette occasion, ils ont une nouvelle fois plaidé en faveur d'un dialogue politique inclusif pour tenter de sortir le pays de la crise politique. Précisions d’Aurélie…
